batches.firstSpokenLine: Welcome to Module 10 — Sanitation and Reset Systems. Build a sanitation system that holds up all day.
batches.lastSpokenLine: …only where it's specifically required. Disinfected is not the same as sterile, and not every Head Spa setup requires sterilization equipment.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Section 10.2 — Process the Right Item the Right Way. Match the process to what the item actually is.
batches.lastSpokenLine: …This is a maintenance tip, not a required procedure — it doesn't replace any disinfection step your system actually requires.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Section 10.3 — Build a Reset Around What Cannot Be Rushed. Contain. Clean. Disinfect. Reset. Verify.
batches.lastSpokenLine: …the required process itself never gets shortened because the next client is waiting.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Reset Under Pressure — the room isn't fully ready, and the next client already is.
batches.lastSpokenLine: Choose the response you think best handles this.

batches.firstSpokenLine: This preserves the required process. The client can wait a few minutes, you can keep working on other reset tasks in parallel, or you can use an already-clean, ready alternative if one exists — the process finishes on its own schedule, not the client's.
batches.lastSpokenLine: This preserves the required process. The client can wait a few minutes, you can keep working on other reset tasks in parallel, or you can use an already-clean, ready alternative if one exists — the process finishes on its own schedule, not the client's.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Wiping it dry because it looks clean skips the actual requirement. Visual cleanliness is not the same as a completed disinfectant contact time or equipment process.
batches.lastSpokenLine: Wiping it dry because it looks clean skips the actual requirement. Visual cleanliness is not the same as a completed disinfectant contact time or equipment process.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Skipping the remaining contact time defeats the reason the process exists. The client arriving early doesn't change what the product or equipment actually requires.
batches.lastSpokenLine: Skipping the remaining contact time defeats the reason the process exists. The client arriving early doesn't change what the product or equipment actually requires.

batches.firstSpokenLine: An unprocessed backup hasn't gone through cleaning or disinfection yet — using it introduces exactly the risk the reset process exists to prevent.
batches.lastSpokenLine: An unprocessed backup hasn't gone through cleaning or disinfection yet — using it introduces exactly the risk the reset process exists to prevent.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Starting the service before the process finishes and catching up afterward reverses the order that keeps the room and tools safe for the next step. The process comes first.
batches.lastSpokenLine: Starting the service before the process finishes and catching up afterward reverses the order that keeps the room and tools safe for the next step. The process comes first.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Section 10.4 — Build the System Before You're Under Pressure. Reduce decisions. Not standards.
batches.lastSpokenLine: …An annual internal review is a reasonable business habit, not a guarantee of compliance on its own.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Section 10.5 — When Routine Reset Is Not Enough. Blood or body fluid is not a routine reset.
batches.lastSpokenLine: …plus a fillable page for recording your own verified product, equipment, and jurisdiction details.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Here's your first checkpoint — between-client reset reasoning. Walk me through your between-client reset in the order that works for your setup.
batches.lastSpokenLine: Take your time, and answer below.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Here's your final checkpoint — post-service concern response. A client contacts you the next day and reports a rash on her neck after the service.
batches.lastSpokenLine: Take your time, and answer below.

batches.firstSpokenLine: Module complete. You can deliver a great service. You can reset it cleanly. That discipline is what makes the experience repeatable — for every client, every time.
batches.lastSpokenLine: …Modern practitioners are already encountering AI — this module teaches you to use it well, without losing the judgment that makes you a professional.
